one_pager.big_idea: A good investigation is planned before anyone touches the kit: a testable question, a fair comparison, a sample size we can justify, and care for safety and for the people who take part.
goals: I can turn a claim into a testable question and plan a fair test with variables, controls and a justified sample size.
I can plan ethically for human participants (voluntary, no pressure, anonymised) and write a specific risk assessment.

flow.what: Two retrieval questions answered on the back of the worksheet: what is an operational definition; turn 'A lid keeps a cup of water warm for longer' into a testable question ('Does ___ change ___?'). Teacher puts a claim card set, planning frame, peer check and approval slip on each table. Slides 1 to 2.

Reveal the claim bank of twelve claims: 'Which claim do you think will be busted?' Plan B: the four snowflake claims (1, 2, 5, 6) are not available, eight remain. Students read the cards and privately tick a top three on the worksheet. Slide 3.

Walk through the planning frame with the model plan ('A lid keeps a cup of water warm for longer'): question, variables, operational definition, sample size with a reason (objects: 3 of each condition, 2 minimum), ethics for testing people, risk table ('Be careful' is too vague), results table. Students point to each box on their own frame. Slides 4 to 8.

Choosing (3 min): groups write a ranked top three on the approval slip; teacher allocates claims (no more than 2 groups per claim) and announces them. Planning (12 min): all write at once in roles on the A3 frame, safety and ethics boxes first; teacher checks safety and ethics and starts approval conversations. Peer check (3 min): groups 1 and 2, 3 and 4, 5 and 6 swap plans and use the checklist. Slides 9 to 10. If short: allocate claims from top threes during the Hook.

Ethics quick-fire, OK or Not OK with a reason, on four scenarios (2 min; A, B and D not OK, C OK); 3 minutes to fix 'Not yet' items while the teacher signs approval slips; exit ticket (2 min); logbook line (1 min). Slides 11 to 12. If short: two scenarios only.

one_pager.practical: No practical work: a planning lesson. Each group chooses a claim from the claim bank (12 claims in Plan A, 8 in Plan B), completes the planning frame in roles, has it checked by a partner group and gets the teacher's signed approval slip.
one_pager.assessment: An approved plan (planning frame plus signed approval slip) for every group: the main evidence for rubric strand 2 (Planning), supporting strand 1 (Questioning). Exit ticket: testable question, one control with a reason, one ethics rule. Logbook line: 'Our claim is ___. We will test it by ___.'
hazards: Plans must copy in the bilingual safety lines from the kit card that match the claim: ice and salt baths (gloves; handle tubes and cups, never the mixture), warm water prepared and poured by the teacher only (no hotter than about 60 °C), no eating or drinking.
Human participants (claims 7, 8, 9 and 12): taking part is voluntary, no pressure, codes not names, anyone can stop or withdraw their results.
Do not approve any plan that involves eating, drinking or tasting, health or diet claims, or anything about named people. Only claims from the bank.
one_pager.language_note: Frames: 'Does ___ change ___?' 'We will change ___, measure ___ in ___ (units), and keep ___ the same.' 'We will test ___ for each condition, because ___.' 'A hazard is ___. It could ___. We will ___.' 'Taking part is voluntary, so we will ___.' Chinese talk is welcome while choosing and planning; boxes are written with key words in English; short notes, not full sentences. Traps: 'control' can mean a control variable (kept the same) or a control group or condition (for comparison); 'hazard' is the thing, 'risk' is what could happen and how likely; 'anonymous' and 'anonymised' are close enough at this level.
watch_out: Choosing eats the planning time: allocate claims quickly and firmly; groups that cannot agree get their highest shared choice; no more than 2 groups per claim.
'More is always better, so we will test 100 cups': sample size must fit the time and kit (3 per condition for objects, 2 minimum; about 18 minutes next week).

Claim 12 needs data from two times of day: only allocate it if a supervised 5-minute slot at the other time can be arranged; otherwise 'start vs end of the lesson', reported as a different, weaker question.
'Ethics only matters for medical tests' and 'friends do not need to be asked': any test with people needs consent, no pressure and codes; ask everyone the same way.
one_pager.next_week_link: Week 8 is investigation day: every group needs a signed approval slip and its tray ready before students arrive. Build the Week 8 kit list from the approval slip stubs and collect kit for each approved claim (thermometers, warm water, scales, puzzles, bottles, fabric); in Plan A, order ice for groups doing claims 1, 2, 5 or 6. Plans not approved in the lesson are approved or annotated within two days. Approved plans are handed back at the start of Week 8.

Confirm, and say whether spares are wanted (none stated).

Claim bank cards: the print spec in Y9_W07_Choose_your_claim.md says '6 sets per class', but the kit card has Recorders count the cards back into the envelope. Are the 6 sets reused for every class (entered as 6 sets, 1 per group)? The envelopes (6 implied) appear only in the clean-up line, not in any kit list.

Safety lines: the lesson plan and Slide 8 tell groups to copy the safety lines 'from the kit card', but the designed kit card (Kit-card.dc.html, Kit-card-2.dc.html) is a single 'Teacher copy'. Print 6 group copies of the kit card (or its back), or show the lines on a slide?
Approval slips: '6 per class (one per group), plus spares' with no number of spares (6 entered). Planning frames: the kit card says 1 per group, the print spec says 6 plus 2 spares (8 entered).

Planning frame on A4: the print spec says 'two sides of A4', but the timeline says all roles write at once 'on the two A4 halves'. One double-sided sheet or two separate sheets (Planning-frame-A4-1.dc.html, Planning-frame-A4-2.dc.html)?

Teacher Guide prep calendar (Week 6 row) lists only claim bank cards and planning frames for Week 7; the lesson file also needs peer checklists, approval slips, model plan sheets, worksheets and the kit card. The guide should be updated.

Claim 12 needs a second time of day; the file leaves the arrangement to the teacher ('Agree with your teacher how and when'). Who supervises the extra 5-minute slot, and is it the same for every class?
Week 3 ruler-drop method cards and conversion tables, and the Week 4 class data photo: the kit card says 'find' them but not how many to bring, or whether the photo is printed or shown on a device.
Storage: planning frames and approval slips are collected, but the file does not say where they are kept until they are handed back in Week 8 (class box assumed).
The kit card's 'about 30 minutes' of teacher prep is not broken down; the per-task minutes are estimates that add up to 30. Cutting 18 sheets of card into 72 cards for 6 sets may take longer.
